body:
Regarding 3, I'm currently working on it and it seems like the only point where we have to calculate the positions for other layouts is in the api, because we invalidate the getBoardByName query after each edit mode save etc.
It's actually already working great on my local machine. The only thing that I might need to add is, that I also generate an automatic layout based on a smaller amount of columns (because currently it just copies the same positions there

Based on the feedback from @manuel-rw I propose the following changes:
1. Auto Layout automatically gets between 5 and 7 layouts at creation (How the breakpoints and amount of columns look like has to be defined)
2. Custom layout gets a new switch which allows the user to enable automatic sizing & positioning while manually adjusting layouts
 a) If auto size & position is enabled, base layout can be selected

What changes are required for the db etc. I'll have to further analyse, I'll do so in the next few days
Thank you, I think it will be much clearer & easy for the user this way :)

I would propose another change:
The user should be able to choose which layout he can change and is used as base layout. So if the user uses a mobile phone he does not need to change the 10 column layout. There are two possible solutions I currently have:
1. The user can only choose between Mobile and Desktop and has to adjust these specific layouts OR
2. The user can choose any of the available Layouts which however all have a descriptive name and description. 

Additionally the label of the input wouldn't be base layout and rather something like **Edit layout** with the description:
> Choose which of the following layouts you want to configure
@manuel-rw are the above proposed changes okay? Which of them do you prefer? Do you have other ideas?

I think this makes it too difficult again. Too much complexity = user wont understand. I believe the user should configure the default layout and the algorithm does the rest of the work. Most people configure their board on desktop anyway.

>  configure the default layout and the algorithm does the rest of the work.   

Definitely the way to go. Personally I would add this selection in the onboarding as a last step to jump-start with a dashboard instead of "create your first board" . You select the design one you think looks the best and it creates a default dashboard with that layout (already populated with many default apps/integrations/widgets) 

Mobile should be secondary as it is 20.2% of traffic (from umami avg 7 days). Mobile is too narrow to be ordered properly, just make the widgets be at top one after the other and each takes the full width of the device. Then scroll below to see the apps in a grid manner respective to the screen's width
